title: Adalina: Adaptive Linear Approximation for the Shapley Value and Beyond
claim: Paired sampling consistently lowers approximation error by a large margin, while the choice of sampling distribution matters comparatively little.
layout: 2x4 grid of log-log line plots, shared axes, legends inside panels
description: A 2x4 grid of log-log line plots. Each panel plots relative approximation error, ||φ̂ − φ||₂/||φ||₂, on the y-axis against the number of utility queries per player (10¹ to 10³) on the x-axis. Each panel has three colored curves: kernel (blue), leverage (orange) and geomean (green), with shaded confidence bands. Solid lines are without paired sampling and dashed lines are with paired sampling. Every curve slopes down as the query budget grows. In most panels the dashed group sits clearly below the solid group, and the three sampling distributions are close to each other within each group. The bottom-row panels show smaller gaps, and the last one shows a different ordering. Legends sit in different corners of the panels. The top row is for positive utilities and the bottom row is for utilities that can be positive or negative.
caption: The relative approximation error of unbiased kernelSHAP in approximating the Shapley value with different sampling distributions. Here, $\lambda = \frac{u_{[n]}-u_{\emptyset}}{n}$. The dashed lines correspond to those with paired sampling, whereas the solid lines are without paired sampling. For the first row, the utility function there is positive, whereas for the second row, $U(S)$ can be either positive or negative.
abstract: The Shapley value, and its broader family of semi-values, has received much attention in various attribution problems. A fundamental and long-standing challenge is their efficient approximation, since exact computation generally requires an exponential number of utility queries in the number of players $n$. To meet the challenges of large-scale applications, we explore the limits of efficiently approximating semi-values under a $Î(n)$ space constraint. Building upon a vector concentration inequality, we establish a theoretical framework that enables sharper query complexities for existing unbiased randomized algorithms. Within this framework, we systematically develop a linear-space algorithm that requires $O(\frac{n}{Îµ^{2}}\log\frac{1}Î´)$ utility queries to ensure $P(\|\hat{\boldsymbolÏ}-\boldsymbolÏ\|_{2}\geqÎµ)\leq Î´$ for all commonly used semi-values. In particular, our framework naturally bridges OFA, unbiased kernelSHAP, SHAP-IQ and the regression-adjusted approach, and definitively characterizes when paired sampling is beneficial. Moreover, our algorithm allows explicit minimization of the mean squared error $\mathbb{E}[\|\hat{\boldsymbolÏ}-\boldsymbolÏ\|_{2}^{2}]$ for each specific utility function. Accordingly, we introduce the first adaptive, linear-time, linear-space randomized algorithm, Adalina, that theoretically achieves improved mean squared error. All of our theoretical findings are experimentally validated. Our code is available at https://github.com/watml/adalina.
